purpose: An expository comparison, preserving source-qualified internal statuses rather than granting new proof acceptance.

references.title: A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions
The Dirichlet problem for a complex Monge–Ampère equation
Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes
The Mabuchi geometry of finite energy classes
A variational approach to complex Monge–Ampère equations
Monge–Ampère operators, Lelong numbers and intersection theory

items.title: Local regularization
items.classical: On relatively compact coordinate subdomains, psh functions admit decreasing smooth psh regularizations.
items.internal: Locally bounded classical psh potentials admit decreasing semipositive rational PL approximation over the original field, on one fixed ordinary neighbourhood.
items.boundary: The decreasing approximants are rational PL; continuous stages also admit smooth positive approximation. This does not classify all current-positive functions as classical psh.
items.scope: The fixed-neighbourhood construction retains the original finite extension \(K/\mathbf Q_p\) and its norm. The separate continuous current-positive regularization input has its own algebraic analytification hypotheses; it is not silently identified with this result.

items.title: Mixed products and continuity
items.classical: Locally bounded psh potentials have positive, symmetric mixed products against a fixed positive closed current, with decreasing continuity.
items.internal: The fixed-background calculus is positive, separately closed, symmetric and local, with CLN estimates and weighted joint decreasing continuity.
items.boundary: The weight is also a decreasing classical psh potential. Discontinuous potentials with an arbitrary moving background are not covered.
items.scope: The background is fixed, symmetric, middle-positive and separately d′- and d″-closed. The original compact smooth CLD tests are retained. The theorem includes the undifferentiated psh weight; it is not continuity for arbitrary moving Borel weights.

items.title: Intrinsic products
items.classical: Where defined, non-pluripolar products depend on the currents, not on the choice of their local potentials.
items.internal: Individual curvature independence is proved. Continuous-coefficient degree-one relations and quadratic relations of joint residue rank at most two are handled.
items.boundary: Full analytic-relation descent remains open. It is an additional quotient problem, not simply the classical change-of-potential theorem.
items.scope: The low-rank result concerns finite presentations in any ambient dimension. In the supplied normal-three models, the punctured action and central spherical pairing are established; cancellation of that pairing is not yet proved in general.

items.title: Capacity and quasicontinuity
items.classical: A psh function is continuous outside open sets of arbitrarily small ambient Bedford–Taylor capacity.
items.internal: Relative quasicontinuity and bounded decreasing convergence in capacity are established for the specified potential class and background.
items.boundary: Relative capacity depends on the background and tester family. It is not automatically the ambient capacity of the complex benchmark.
items.scope: The relative theory uses the full family of normalized classical psh testers, not a selected finite test family. The ambient S=[1] theory and arbitrary-background relative theory are kept distinct.

items.title: Borel regularity and extremals
items.classical: On bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains, ambient outer capacity is Choquet; compact capacity equals the extremal Monge–Ampère mass.
items.internal: The qualified ambient Choquet theory is available. Relative inner regularity is proved for specified finite-Hausdorff saturated sets and controlled backgrounds.
items.boundary: Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity remains open. Universal raw-to-outer equality and extremal total-mass formulas are false.
items.scope: The relative positive case has remaining degree q=1 on a torus box, with S₀=βⁿ⁻¹[X] and fully saturated inverse images of Borel moment sets of finite (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure, plus the stated one-sided background comparison. It is not a theorem for arbitrary Borel sets. Classical Borel capacitability is compact inner regularity of outer capacity; that is the open target, not raw=outer on every set.

items.title: Polar sets and comparison
items.classical: On bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains, ambient outer-null sets are pluripolar. Bounded psh functions satisfy comparison and domination with boundary hypotheses.
items.internal: For S=[1], local polar, outer-null and negligible sets coincide. Compact-boundary-gap comparison and the specified relative domination principles are proved.
items.boundary: An arbitrary background may charge ambient polar sets. Pointwise detection from a relative capacity class needs additional geometry.
items.scope: The S=[1] equivalence is local; the Choquet and extremal package retains its exhaustion-domain assumptions. The relative domination proposition initially gives a raw-capacity conclusion: it must not be relabelled as outer-null without an additional argument.

items.title: Unbounded, non-polar products
items.classical: On compact Kähler manifolds, non-pluripolar products are well-defined and closed. Monotone Monge–Ampère continuity is available in the full-mass class.
items.internal: Common truncations yield closed non-polar products when coefficient masses are locally finite. In the stated boundary class, no loss is characterized by a capacity tail.
items.boundary: The local relative construction does not automatically supply the global compact-Kähler finiteness package. Finiteness and no-loss assumptions matter on both sides.
items.scope: Within the stated zero-boundary class, no loss is equivalent to \(t^q C_S(\{u<-t\};V)\to0\). The negative sublevels must have ordinary closures compact in V. Closedness belongs to the locally coefficient-finite limit, not necessarily to each restricted truncation current. BEGZ Example 1.3 also excludes unrestricted local unbounded products in complex geometry.

items.title: Finite energy and completion
items.classical: On a compact connected Kähler manifold, \((\mathcal E^1,d_1)\) is the metric completion of smooth Kähler potentials.
items.internal: Power-energy classes and mixed Green–Hölder estimates are constructed. The relative strong first-energy completion has an intrinsic Borel realization and is complete.
items.boundary: Canonical ambient classical psh representatives and extension beyond the specified domains remain separate problems; the completion alone does not supply them.
items.scope: The domain is a strict Laurent box with closure compact inside an affinoid interior and a background extending to an ordinary neighbourhood of that closure. Strong convergence is capacity convergence plus energy convergence. All positive power classes and the stated weighted-current degree budgets are retained. Order completion of currents, strong completion of potentials and capacity-Borel realization are not identified.

items.title: Envelopes and rooftops
items.classical: In a fixed Kähler class, rooftop envelopes contract \(d_1\) and express it through the Aubin–Mabuchi energy.
items.internal: Relative Perron envelopes, finite rooftops and the stated Borel obstacle problems are constructed in the completed cone.
items.boundary: The fixed-background ordered-rooftop estimates proposed for literal-dual continuity are still a route to prove, not a consequence of existence.
items.scope: The envelope uses the relative quasi-everywhere order in the completed cone; it is not automatically ordinary ambient upper-semicontinuous regularization. Darvas’s d₁ formula is not the coefficient-one inequality for the project’s different homogeneous energy.

items.title: Strong integral continuity
items.classical: For \(\mu=\operatorname{MA}(v)\) with \(v\in\mathcal E^1\) in a fixed compact Kähler class, \(d_1\)-convergence implies \(L^1(\mu)\)-convergence.
items.internal: The energy-difference space is Banach. Strong literal integral continuity is proved under fixed-source domination or the stated capacity-control hypotheses.
items.boundary: For fixed S, does global literal energy-dual boundedness imply strong \(L^1(\mu)\)-continuity? The source-class benchmark does not answer this larger question.
items.scope: The question assumes a positive Radon measure annihilating the relative null ideal, literal integrability of every completed Borel difference, and a bounded integral functional on the entire energy-difference Banach space. Total mass need not be finite. Nonliteral functionals, bounds on only one witness sequence, and changing-background examples do not refute this fixed-background question.

items.title: Prescribing a source measure
items.classical: In a fixed compact Kähler class, a normalized finite-energy measure is the Monge–Ampère measure of a unique finite-energy current.
items.internal: The source image is norm closed. Strongly continuous data have a unique variational projection. For such literal positive data, the equation holds exactly when \(\Xi=0\).
items.boundary: Data-side conditions forcing \(\Xi=0\) remain to be found beyond compatible classes. Smooth positive perturbations need not remain in the source image.
items.scope: Here the positive Radon datum defines a literal, norm-bounded integral functional on all completed differences, with a strongly continuous restriction to the cone. The defect is evaluated using the variational projection; its vanishing is an exact criterion, not an independent test already computable from arbitrary data. A variational maximizer need not satisfy the equation in the prescribed potential cone. Source compatibility is separate from strong integral continuity.

items.title: Boundary-value problems
items.classical: On bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains, continuous boundary data and a nonnegative continuous density admit a unique continuous psh Monge–Ampère solution.
items.internal: For remaining degree q=1, finite signed energy-diffuse data have a unique renormalized zero-boundary solution in the faithful part-energy space.
items.boundary: Not the same equation: this is a signed linear problem, not a general nonlinear Monge–Ampère boundary-value theorem.
items.scope: Here q=n−p=1 is the remaining degree, not a restriction to ambient dimension one. The faithful, regular, strongly local, coercive part-form hypotheses and energy-capacity diffuseness are retained. The solution space is not identified with the classical psh cone or the nonlinear strong first-energy cone; clipping and total-variation stability hold in the stated linear space.

obstructions.title: Unconditional relative capacity identities
obstructions.claim: Raw capacity need not equal its outer regularization, even on compact sets. A universal extremal total-mass formula also fails.
obstructions.qualification: This contrasts with the stated ambient complex theorem, not with every complex relative capacity. The ratio in the internal mass example varies with scale.

obstructions.title: Strong subadditivity of relative outer capacity
obstructions.claim: An original torus example with q=1 and n≥2 violates strong subadditivity. Ordinary subadditivity survives.
obstructions.qualification: This does not settle Borel inner regularity. No general classical strong-subadditivity theorem is being asserted here.

obstructions.title: A universal coefficient-one rooftop bound
obstructions.claim: For the project’s rooftop energy inequality in remaining degree one, constant 1 is false; constant 2 is sharp across allowed backgrounds.
obstructions.qualification: The inequality is \(e(P_S(u,v))\leq C(e(u)+e(v))\). This is not Darvas’s d₁ contraction formula. It does not invalidate the mixed Green–Hölder constant 1 or settle fixed-S literal continuity.

obstructions.title: Universal solvability under small smooth perturbations
obstructions.claim: A fixed strict source admits smooth positive density perturbations converging uniformly to 1 that lie outside the strong-completion source image.
obstructions.qualification: These data retain source domination and literal strong continuity. Solving the signed linear equation in a larger part-energy space does not restore a solution in the prescribed cone.
